sample.identification: Obfuscated macOS multi-store credential stealer and payload installer

decision: Counterfeit system-password capture, credential-store staging and uploads, wallet-app replacement and disguised persistence form a coherent attack. No legitimate app purpose or authorization is supplied. Public-registry origin and absence of external corroboration do not explain away these code paths.

methods: atomscan before/after, including seven recovered shell layers
cleave facts: literals, calls, imports, decoded strings and propagation limits
Independent static third-party bytecode decompilation with MessageSend trace comments; no specimen execution
Offline constant folding of 4,081 calls to twelve inspected numeric/hex decoder helpers
Inspected raw helper bytecode: arithmetic -> character-ID object -> concatenation -> local store -> returned local; decompiler return-empty artifacts are not runtime semantics
Compiled a harmless system-attribute control: fndr.gstl is the environment-reading event used for dynamic configuration
independent_second_review.recovery: Reproduced the prior exact-SHA recovery in an independent scratch checkout; the existing payload-reduced.applescript is identical apart from terminal newline layout.

execution_paths.effect: Creates randomized temporary staging, inventories host, recursively copies selected messaging, browser, wallet, password-manager and developer-secret stores. File helpers use cp -f, cat redirection and Finder duplication; omit cache directories.

Reads a cached .auth value; validates with dscl . authonly. Otherwise loops a masked dialog titled System Preferences until the submitted local-account password validates, then caches it and writes staging/pwd. The shell helper and write helper are reachable from the entry point.

On the selected macOS version branch, replays the captured password to unlock login.keychain-db and alter Chrome generic-password partition access for a developer team ID, queries Chrome Safe Storage and stages recovered material. The version test selects secret-access handling; it does not establish VM evasion.

Archives the same staging directory into a hidden UUID-derived ZIP, posts that ZIP in multipart file=@ data to the configured /contact endpoint, retries three times with delay, then tries a separately configured fallback endpoint. Repeats staging/upload across collection phases.

For installed Ledger Wallet, Trezor Suite and Exodus bundles, retrieves a replacement ZIP, checks PK magic and size, kills the wallet process, removes its bundle with captured-password sudo fallback, extracts the replacement to /Applications, adjusts executable permissions and removes the ZIP. These are local app replacements, not evidence of spread to another machine.

Uses captured-password sudo to install root-owned LaunchDaemons with RunAtLoad/KeepAlive; downloads helper files into hidden Apple-style Application Support directories, removes quarantine, and installs a console-user watchdog using launchctl bsexec/asuser. A user LaunchAgent fallback is coded for insufficient privilege.

Optional externally configured payload download, chmod, ad-hoc signing, quarantine removal and execution are coded. Cleanup deletes staged files and ZIP/chunk artifacts. Notification-suppression handlers are also present; no runtime success was tested.

context_limits: No registry package identity, claimed legitimate product purpose, consent or deployment context was supplied.

Configuration endpoints and other values are read from environment attributes; their runtime values are absent from this standalone file. No assumption of successful network transfer, elevation, replacement or persistence is necessary for the verdict.
No recognized malware-family identity rule is added: the behavior resembles macOS stealers, but those capabilities alone do not establish a particular family.

shared_rule_review.change: Firefox and Waterfox profile paths remain notable with the same matchers, scopes and IDs; removed theft/discovery mappings.
shared_rule_review.unsupported_claim: A profile path alone proves neither reading it nor credential theft and does not earn suspicious criticality.
shared_rule_review.consumers: macos-credential-store-targets explicitly selects these IDs, with needs=3. Its membership and threshold remain unchanged; exact-SHA fixture and an independent index.applescript stealer retain their hostile detections.
shared_rule_review.benign_control: waterfox-reference.scpt simply returns a profile path and retains the notable path finding.

shared_rule_review.change: Moved HTTP scheme literal from communications/http/curl to communications/url/scheme; same matcher and AppleScript/macOS scope.
shared_rule_review.unsupported_claim: The sample match is the public HTTP URL in a plist DTD declaration. A URL scheme is not a curl command, network connection or exfiltration.
shared_rule_review.consumers: No exact old-ID consumers. Inspected curl, HTTP and communications directory consumers; the generic HTTP-client rollup should not infer a client from a scheme alone. Non-AppleScript consumers cannot select the former AppleScript-only leaf. Actual curl, upload and stealer observations remain intact.
shared_rule_review.benign_control: scheme-only.scpt retains the scheme at its correct home, without a curl or HTTP-client claim; existing uploader.scpt and independent index.applescript retain all former trait IDs.

shared_rule_review.change: Removed T1041 default from ordinary curl observations, T1083/E1083 defaults from browser-path references, and T1543.004/B0028 from a launchctl command reference.
shared_rule_review.unsupported_claim: HTTP client text does not establish exfiltration; paths do not establish a filesystem survey; a launchctl command reference does not establish collection or durable installation. Matchers, scopes and criticalities are unchanged.

shared_rule_review.change: Telegram composite description now says session target rather than copies tdata.
shared_rule_review.unsupported_claim: Its required Telegram evidence is a path reference, not a bound copy operation. Actual sample copying was independently confirmed; the matcher and hostile coverage are retained.

new_coverage: Repeated compiled arithmetic character reconstruction, independent of helper names and string contents
Compiled dialog-call and hidden-answer-parameter observations; the parameter observation does not assert its Boolean value
Suspicious concealed system-dialog/keychain-query co-occurrence; does not claim resolved result-to-secret data flow
Hostile concealed Apple-style launchd installer: shell execution, HTTP client, sudo password input, launchctl, LaunchDaemons and RunAtLoad/KeepAlive with a hidden Apple-style path
remaining_detection_gaps: The shared facts producer does not evaluate custom numeric-decoder handlers interprocedurally. Individual matcher coverage for the fully concealed password-validation, keychain ACL change, quarantine removal, wallet-app substitution and notification-suppression command chains remains incomplete. Independent reverse engineering establishes those behaviors; no invented commands, duplicate traits or score-tuning workarounds were added.
